sources.details: For each position q, l_q=logsumexp_c(z_qc)-z_q,target_q in natural-log nats. From raw saved float32 scores evaluated in float64: [3.2427700458769175,3.528132585015193,3.236014399990441]; sum/3=3.3356390102941837. No class weights/ignored labels; denominator=3 questions, classes=20. F.cross_entropy differs by 1.0355e-8 and rounds to 3.336.

claims.statement: The eight internal features at each position are a hidden representation; the output/language-model head maps them to vocabulary candidate scores using one weight vector per candidate and is a different function from an attention head.
claims.scope: The eight features are preserved through the local block and final LN; the actual last computation is final_norm then bias-free Linear. 'Language modeling head' describes the output role, not an attention subdivision; no universal claim about tied weights.

evidence.supports: One learnable output row weights H_in features and maps only the last axis; bias=False gives a weighted dot product.
Official wording language modeling head, implemented Linear(hidden,vocab), versus attention.num_heads; hidden_states feed the projection.
The local residual block preserves width and final_norm precedes output Linear.
The local feedforward branch returns the original width after expansion.
Hooked block/final LN both [1,3,8]; final projection equals hidden@weight.T with exactly zero error.

claims.statement: TinyLM(ModelConfig(vocab_size=20,width=8)) accepts one [1,2,3] ID row and returns dict['logits'] with shape [1,3,20] through token/position embedding, block, final LN and output. These are raw scores; argmax(dim=-1) returns one candidate ID per position with shape [1,3]. Its input/output weights are independent trainable tables, and this code only initializes/forwards/calculates a loss.
claims.scope: Exact current repository default config, seed 42 and CPU environment. No tokenizer semantics, trained quality or generic guarantee about all language models. The forward creates an autograd graph but does not itself backward or update weights.

evidence.supports: Default tied=False/layers=1; separate tables; embeddings plus positions; blocks and final norm; raw output projection stored under logits.
Linear preserves batch/position axes and has learnable [20,8] weights.
Embedding adds feature axis with learnable table; supports the [1,3,8] token representation.
argmax selects maxima indices across supplied dimension, keepdim=False.
Unnormalized logits need not be positive or sum to one.
Both original code fences run in order: [1,3,20], guesses [[10,17,7]], loss printed.
Shapes and axes; separate requires_grad storage; negative/unnormalized scores; no update or populated parameter gradients.

verification.expected: [1,3,8] hidden then [1,3,20] raw logits; argmax [1,3]; distinct trainable [20,8] tables; no parameter update.
verification.observed: All expected shapes and storage checks passed. Raw scores range -1.1452488899230957 to 1.211037516593933; argmax [[10,17,7]]; parameters exactly unchanged and grads None.
verification.details: Original two fences used their actual bootstrap and repository imports. Independent hooks and dot-product checks used literal IDs, with no optimizer/backward/checkpoint/dataset.

claims.statement: Rows 0,1,2 can read prefixes [1],[1,2],[1,2,3] and serve different next-ID questions with prescribed targets 2,3,4. Continuation chooses a new ID using only the last row, appends it and repeats the forward computation, rather than appending all three earlier-position guesses.
claims.scope: Inclusive causal attention and this repository's default generate(use_cache=False), with no padding/cache/packing. Target 4 is a prescribed synthetic continuation, not a semantic fact inferred from arbitrary ID numbers. Efficient implementations may cache instead of recomputing full prefixes.

evidence.supports: Original causal mask excludes future positions and output logits have per-position vocabulary predictions.
Original autoregressive sampler uses only logits[:, -1, :] then appends one new token each loop, with a cache.
Local inclusive causal visibility mask, applied before score softmax.
Uncached loop forwards entire current sequence, selects last row, argmaxes and appends one token.
Triangular mask and future-token perturbation/prefix equivalence; captured actual uncached inputs and manual last-row generation comparison.

verification.expected: Mask rows allow only positions <= row; changing future ID leaves earlier outputs unchanged; two steps append only two tokens.
verification.observed: Mask [[T,F,F],[T,T,F],[T,T,T]]; prior-position perturbation error=0; separate prefixes max error<=1.79e-7; forward inputs [1,2,3] then [1,2,3,7]; output [1,2,3,7,6].
verification.details: Prefix float32 comparisons use absolute tolerance 1e-6. Generation max_new_tokens=2,use_cache=False,eos_id=-1 prevents an early synthetic EOS; it exactly matches two manual final-row argmax steps.

claims.statement: Reshaping [1,3,20] to [3,20] and targets [1,3] to [3] preserves row/label order, yields three cross-entropy questions with labels 2,3,4, and the initialized mean cost is about 3.336.
claims.scope: Only the seed-42 random model and exact repo code on the recorded CPU version. Mean is unweighted over three nonignored labels in natural-log nats/question; it does not demonstrate learned answers or model accuracy.

evidence.supports: reshape retains data/element count and infers the -1 dimension.
Cross entropy accepts (N,C)/(N) class-index inputs and defaults to mean, no smoothing, ignore_index=-100.
Class-index negative-log probability and weighted nonignored mean; specializes to sum of three losses divided by 3 here.
Exact original initialized CE=3.335638999938965.
Exact row identity, preserved labels, independent float64 logsumexp calculation, changed-label variation and round-to-three-decimals test.

evidence.supports: Three independent per-question calculations produce 3.3356390102941837 nats/question.

verification.expected: Exactly [3,20]/[3], label order [2,3,4], denominator=3 and mean rounds to 3.336.
verification.details: Every flattened row is exactly equal to its original position. -1=(1*3*20)/20=3; answers flatten to 3 labels. No ignored labels, weights or smoothing; 20 is candidate count, not loss denominator.
verification.tolerance: Shape/row/label checks exact; absolute CE versus float64 tolerance 1e-6 (observed 1.0355e-8); display 3.336 checked by rounding to three decimals (0.0005 rounding unit).

claims.statement: Changing vocab_size from 20 to 25 with the same input gives [1,3,25], five additional candidate scores at each position and possibly different initialized argmax IDs; for vocab_size=20 the legal input IDs are 0–19 and ID20 is out of range.
claims.scope: This repo uses integer embedding lookup and separately initializes the model for each configuration. The output shape increase is guaranteed by configuration; the observed changed guesses are a local example, not a guarantee of change for every initialization.

evidence.supports: num_embeddings determines dictionary rows; embeddings preserve input shape plus feature axis.
Embedding row count V equals maximum possible index+1.
out_features determines last output axis, including vocabulary size.
Both input table and output projection use configured vocab_size; forward starts with input lookup.
Executed vocab=25 shape/count/argmax variation and legal/illegal indices.
